title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Part II of the 'Longue Marche' sequel ('variations sur l'équation des lacets'), §VI-VII. Grothendieck is building a 'modular pinning' of twisted forms G of GL(2) over a base S (forms attached to a rank-4 Azumaya algebra M), together with SG and PG. The pinning uses the images of the standard generators of SL(2,Z), the fundamental group of the modular orbifold M_{1,1}, rather than a torus-plus-root-vector pinning in the sense of SGA3.

The previous page defines a modular triple in PG. This page defines a modular triple in G: sections (rho, sigma, eps0) of G satisfying the following.

(52) eps0 = -sigma^{-1} rho, equivalently rho^{-1} sigma eps0 = -1. Equivalently -rho sigma^{-1} = eps1, with eps1 := rho eps0 rho^{-1} = sigma eps0 sigma^{-1}.

(53) (rho+sigma)^2 = rho+sigma, i.e. rho+sigma is an idempotent.

(54) eps0 = 1 + N0 is regular unipotent: Tr N0 = det N0 = 0 and N0 is nonzero in every fibre. The margin gives the equivalent form det eps0 = 1, Tr eps0 = 2, eps0 ≠ 1 fibrewise. This is equivalent to eps1 being regular unipotent.

(55) eps0 and eps1 are 'inequivalent' in every fibre, i.e. N0 and N1 are nowhere homothetic. In other words, they define distinct unipotent lines (distinct cusps).

(56) One of four equivalent conditions holds: sigma^2 + 1 = 0; rho^2 - rho + 1 = 0; Tr sigma = 0 and det sigma = 1; Tr rho = det rho = 1.

Point 3 defines the standard triple in GL(2)_S:
- rho0 = [[0,1],[-1,1]] (order 6, rho0^3 = -1);
- sigma0 = [[0,-1],[1,0]] (order 4, sigma0^2 = -1);
- eps0 = [[1,-1],[0,1]].
Its image in PGL(2) = GP(1)_S is the projective standard triple. The page asserts it is indeed a modular triple. It then announces the canonical maps phi ↦ (phi(rho0), phi(sigma0), phi(eps0)), from Isom(GL(2),G) to Tripmod(G) and from Isom(PGL(2),PG) to Tripmod(PG). The next page states the 'théorème d'épinglage': all arrows in this square are bijective.

Modern reading: the functor of isomorphisms GL2 → G (a GL2-torsor, given Aut(GL2)) is represented by the scheme of 'modular triples'. These are images of S and ST-type generators of SL(2,Z) = <s,r | s^4 = 1, s^2 = r^3>, normalised so that the cusp element is a regular unipotent with distinct conjugate cusp. Injectivity amounts to the intersection of the centralizers of rho and sigma being the centre.

Role in the larger project: rigidify forms of GL2 (e.g. coming from elliptic-curve monodromy / the Teichmüller tower, M_{1,1}) by a level-1 modular datum, so that SL(2,Z)-type data and the 'loop equation' can be transported to arbitrary forms over S.
errors: No error in the stated identities; I checked them on the standard triple. -sigma0^{-1} rho0 = [[1,-1],[0,1]] = eps0. rho0 eps0 rho0^{-1} = [[1,0],[1,1]] = -rho0 sigma0^{-1} = eps1 (agreeing with (48) on the previous page). rho0 + sigma0 = diag(0,1), which is idempotent. Tr rho0 = det rho0 = 1 and sigma0^2 = -1.

Redundancy: given (52) and (56), condition (53) is equivalent to Tr eps0 = 2. By the polarized Cayley-Hamilton identity, (rho+sigma)^2 = rho+sigma reduces to Tr(rho sigma) = 2, and Tr(rho sigma) = -Tr(sigma^2 eps0) = Tr eps0. Since det eps0 = 1 is automatic from (56), (53) only encodes unipotence and not regularity. It is therefore partly redundant with (54). The '~> unipotent régulier' arrow suggests Grothendieck saw this but did not prune the list.

Terminology tension with the previous page: there, (51) asks the eps-tilde to be 'homologues/équivalents' fibrewise. Here, (55) asks eps0 and eps1 to be 'inéquivalents', meaning N0 and N1 are non-homothetic. Over a field all regular unipotents are conjugate, so 'équivalent' must mean 'same unipotent line'. The two pages' wording is inconsistent, or one of them was being revised.
The word 'cinq' (five conditions) is not quite accurate. There are five numbered conditions, but (52)-(56) include alternatives and equivalent reformulations.

ideas.what: Pinning a twisted form of GL2/PGL2 by a 'modular triple' (images of the SL(2,Z) generators of orders 4 and 6 and the cusp unipotent). Isom(GL2,G) ≅ Tripmod(G) and Isom(PGL2,PG) ≅ Tripmod(PG).
ideas.modern_name: Rigidification of forms (torsor trivialization) via a representation of the modular group; non-standard épinglage
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard épinglages (torus + root vectors): Demazure-Grothendieck, SGA3. The 'modular' version: no standard attribution known to me.
ideas.where_published: Unpublished notes, Longue Marche part II (Montpellier 140-3); not in SGA3 in this form as far as I know.

ideas.what: Characterization of the cusp unipotent via the idempotence (rho+sigma)^2 = rho+sigma.
ideas.modern_name: Polarized Cayley-Hamilton trace identity for 2x2 matrices

ideas.what: Equivalences sigma^2 = -1 ⇔ (Tr sigma = 0, det sigma = 1), and rho^2 - rho + 1 = 0 ⇔ (Tr rho = det rho = 1).
ideas.modern_name: Cayley-Hamilton; elliptic elements of orders 4 and 6 in SL2

ideas.what: Injectivity of the pinning map amounts to the centralizers of rho and sigma meeting only in the centre (stated on the next page).
ideas.modern_name: Zariski density / irreducibility of the modular-group image; trivial centralizer of the representation

missed.claim: A scheme-theoretic 'modular pinning' of arbitrary forms of GL2/PGL2 (Azumaya rank 4) over any base S. The isomorphism torsor is represented by triples satisfying explicit polynomial identities modelled on SL(2,Z) = Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6. It is presumably meant to transport the Teichmüller-tower / M_{1,1} 'loop equation' to twisted forms. I know of no published treatment of exactly this rigidification, but mathematically it is elementary.
missed.quote: Appelons triplet modulaire standard dans GL(2)_S (resp. dans GP(1)_S) le triplet (ρ0 = (0 1;-1 1), σ0 = (0 -1;1 0), ε0 = (1 -1;0 1))
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is documentation of how Grothendieck intended to make the SL(2,Z)/M_{1,1} part of the Teichmüller tower functorial over arbitrary bases and twisted forms. It is of historical interest for Grothendieck-Teichmüller and anabelian work on M_{1,1}, rather than a new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful, essentially elementary rigidification lemma inside Grothendieck's larger unpublished project. The 'modular pinning' formulation is a nice unpublished detail, but any specialist could reconstruct it quickly. It has no deep content beyond Cayley-Hamilton and the trivial centralizer of the SL(2,Z) image.
transcription_corrections: The heading '333)' is the item number '3)' (overwritten digits), not a page number; the page number 333 is at the bottom left.

In (55), the parenthetical reads approximately '(⟺ N0 et N1 non homothétiques en ttes fibres)', not 'non bornés'. The main clause is approximately 'ε0 et ε1 sont inéquivalents en chaque fibre', with a crossed-out ρ before ε0.
In (54), the margin note (with a double arrow pointing to (54)) reads: 'det ε0 = 1, Tr ε0 = 2, ε0 ≠ 1 en ttes fibres'.
In (54), the text reads 'N0 non nul en chaque fibre'.
After (53), the text reads '↝ unipotent régulier i.e. ε0 = 1 + N0 avec'.
'GP(1)_S' and 'Γ GP(1)_S' are probably 'GPl(1)_S' (= PGL(2)) and 'Γ(GPl(1)_S)' (sections), consistent with the next page.
The last lines read 'Ceci posé, on a les diagrammes commut. des applications canoniques'.
